chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. All praise is to Allah, the One, the Almighty, the Honorable, the Powerful, the Merciful, the Forgiver, the Originator of the Earth and the Heaven, the Creator of darkness and light, the Determiner of times and ages, the Manager of causes and affairs, the Resurrector of those in the graves, the Informed of what is apparent and hidden, the Knowing of what has passed and what is distant. To Him belongs the grace, the authority, the strength, and the capability. I praise Him in all states, and I seek guidance from Him for the best of deeds, and I seek refuge in Him from deviation and misguidance.
And I thank Him with a thanksgiving that earns more favor and fulfills the promises, and I seek His help for what saves from destruction and threat.

And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, the First, who is not described as having a beginning, and the Last, who is not described as having an end, the Guide, who remains and endures, and knows the secret and what is more hidden.

And I bear witness that Muhammad is His honored servant and His trustworthy Messenger, known for his obedience, chosen for intercession. For indeed He sent him to establish justice over the crooked, and He sent him to place the Proofs, so that he may be a mercy for the believers and a proof against the disbelievers, and supported by the marked angels, until Allah made His religion apparent despite the polytheists' dislike. May Allah's blessings be upon him and his pure family.
And I bear witness that Ali ibn Abi Talib is the Commander of the Faithful, the Master of the Muslims, and the Caliph of the Messenger of the Worlds.

And I bear witness that the Imams from his offspring are the Proofs of Allah until the Day of Recompense, and the inheritors of the knowledge of the Prophets. May Allah's blessings, mercy, peace, and grace be upon them all.
ai.seo_question: What is the theological declaration of faith in the foreword of Uyun Akhbar al-Rida?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq, this foreword establishes the theological foundation of the book by linking the divine attributes of Allah directly to the institution of Imamate, presenting the Ahl al-Bayt as the living proofs (Hujaj) of God. It reflects the distinct Shia emphasis on the continuity of divine guidance through the progeny of Ali ibn Abi Talib, framing the Imams not merely as successors but as the ultimate authority for interpreting faith after the Prophet.
